issues.description: Compile RPC ships the full script content in its response instead of exposing a dedicated download endpoint.
issues.detail: The backend wrote the file to disk and already returns its path; embedding the entire compiled script in every compile_notebook response inflates memory and bandwidth for a payload only sometimes consumed, and silently broadens the RPC's contract. Add a separate read_script(path) or download RPC and have the frontend fetch on click.

issues.description: open(script_path) lacks explicit encoding and post-success error handling.
issues.detail: The read relies on the platform's default encoding and has no guard against IO errors after compile_pipeline succeeded. A locale mismatch or transient read failure will poison the whole RPC result. Specify encoding='utf-8' and either handle the read failure or move the read out of the success path.

issues.description: Download icon renders unconditionally while handler guards on compiledContent, producing silent no-op clicks.
issues.detail: The icon is always shown in the success branch, but handleDownloadClick bails when compiledContent is absent (older backend, partial response, future caller). Users get a click with no feedback. Gate rendering on compiledContent's presence at the type level, or disable the affordance when missing.

issues.description: GetAppIcon used as an interactive click target instead of a real button.
issues.detail: The SVG icon has onClick and a title but no role, no keyboard handler, and no focus ring, making it inaccessible to keyboard and screen-reader users. Wrap it in an IconButton or anchor with appropriate aria-label so it matches the surrounding 'Done' link's affordance.

issues.description: compiledContent added to DeployProgressState without a documented lifetime or size contract.
issues.detail: The state gains a raw string field with no JSDoc stating when it is set, when cleared, who owns disposal, or what bounds its size; both compiledPath and compiledContent are then prop-drilled through four files when one would do. Document the invariant and collapse the duplicated state.

issues.description: Object URL and DOM anchor not revoked on exception paths in handleDownloadClick.
issues.detail: If a.click() throws under CSP or sandboxing, the synthetic anchor is never removed and the Blob object URL is never revoked, leaking resources. Wrap the create-anchor-click-revoke dance in try/finally so cleanup holds unconditionally, and add a brief comment explaining the idiom.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the feature works but the data shape is wrong: shipping the entire compiled script through the compile_notebook RPC response broadens the contract, wastes memory, and couples compile to download. The backend read lacks an explicit UTF-8 encoding and post-success error handling, so a locale or IO hiccup can poison a successful compile. The download icon renders without gating on the content it needs, producing silent no-op clicks, and the SVG-as-button violates accessibility. Secondary concerns: undocumented state lifetime with prop-drilled duplication, and missing try/finally cleanup of the object URL. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK before merge — extract a dedicated download endpoint and tighten the contracts.
